text.S1: Near a great forest dwelt a poor woodcutter with his wife and his two children. The boy was called Hansel and the girl Gretel.
text.S2: Near a great forest dwelt a poor woodcutter with his wife and his two children. The boy was called Hansel and the girl Gretel.
text.T1: Pafupi ndi nkhalango yaikulu pamakhala wotema nkhuni ndi mkazi wake ndi ana ake awiri.Mnyamata dzina lake linali Hensel ndipo dzina la mtsikana linali Gretel.
text.T2: Pafupi ndi nkhalango yaikulu pamakhala wotema nkhuni wosauka ndi mkazi wake ndi ana ake awiri.Mnyamata dzina lake linali Hensel ndipo dzina la mtsikana linali Gretel.

text.S1: He had little to bite and to break, and when great scarcity fell on the land, he could no longer procure daily bread. Now when he thought over this at night in his bed, and tossed about in his anxiety...
text.S2: He didn’t have enough food, and when great scarcity fell on the land, he could no longer procure daily bread. Now when he thought over this at night in his bed, and tossed about in his anxiety...
text.T1: Iye anali anali ndi cakudya cosakwanira,ndipo pamene njala inayamba m’dziko,samakwanitsa kupeza cakudya catsiku ndi tsiku.Ndipo pamene anaganizirapo usiku wonse ali gone pa kama lake, ndipo anasandamuka ali ndi nkhawa yake...
text.T2: Iye analibe cakudya cokwanira,ndipo pamene njala inayamba m’dziko,samakwanitsa kupeza cakudya catsiku ndi tsiku.Ndipo pamene anaganizirapo usiku wonse ali gone pa kama lake, ndipo anasandamuka ali ndi nkhawa yake...

text.S1: He groaned and said to his wife, “What is to become of us? How are we to feed our poor children, when we no longer have anything even for ourselves?”
text.S2: He groaned and said to his wife, “What is to become of us? How are we to feed our poor children, when we no longer have anything even for ourselves?”
text.T1: Iye anakuwira mkazi wake kuti “Kodi n’ciyani cidzacititika kwa ife? Kodi tidzadyetsa bwanji ana athu, pamene tilibe cakudya ngakhale ife?”
text.T2: Iye anabuula ndi kunena kwa mkazi wake kuti “Kodi n’ciyani cidzacitika kwa ife? Kodi tidzadyetsa bwanji ana athu, pamene tilibe cakudya ngakhale ife omwe?”

text.S1: “I'll tell you what, husband,” answered the woman, “Early tomorrow morning we will take the children out into the forest where it is the thickest. There we will light a fire for them, and give each of them one piece of bread, and then we will go to our work and leave them alone. They will not find the way home again, and we shall be rid of them.”
text.S2: “I'll tell you what, husband,” answered the woman, “Early tomorrow morning we will take the children out into the forest where it is the thickest. There we will light a fire for them, and give each of them one piece of bread, and then we will go to our work and leave them alone. They will not find the way home again, and we shall be rid of them.”
text.T1: “Ndidzakuwuzani cinacake, amuna anga, anayankha mkazi wake, “Mawa m’mamawa tidatenga ana athu ndikupita nawo m’nkhalango komwe kuli mitengo yambiri. Tidzawatsira moto, ndipo aliyense tidzamupatsa buledi m’modzi, ndipo ife tidzapita kunchito yathu ndi kuwasiya okha. Sadzakwanitsa kubwerera kunyumba, ndipondi mmene adzafera”
text.T2: “Ndidzakuwuzani cinacake, amuna anga, anayankha mkazi wake, “Mawa m’mamawa tidzatenga ana athu ndikupita nawo m’nkhalango komwe kuli mitengo yambiri. text.S1: “No,wife,” said the man, “I will not do that; how can I bear to leave my children alone in the forest?-the wild animals would soon come and tear them to pieces.”
text.S2: “No,wife,” said the man, “I will not do that; how can I bear to leave my children alone in the forest?-the wild animals would soon come and tear them to pieces.”

text.T2: “Iyayi mkazi wanga,” anatero mwamuna, “Sindingacite cimeneci; zingatheke bwanji kukhala ndi ana ndipo pambuyo pake kuwasiya m’nkhalango?- nyama zamthengo zingabwere msanga ndi kuwang’amba ndikuwasiya zidutswa.”

text.S1: “O, you fool!” said she, “Then we must all four die of hunger. You maynas well plane the planks for our coffins,” and she left him no peace until he consented. “But I feel very sorry for the poor children, all the same,” said the man.

text.T1: “O, citsiru iwe, Anati, ‘ndiye tonse anayi tiyenera kufa ndi njala, Mukhozanso kupanga matabwa a mabokosi ath ndipo sanamulole kuti akhale ndi mtendere mpaka atavomera “Koma ndikumva cisoni kwambiri ndi ana osaukawa, cimodzimodzi, adatero bamboyo.
text.T2: “O, citsiru iwe, Anati, ‘ndiye tonse anayi tiyenera kufa ndi njala, Mukhozanso kupanga matabwa a mabokosi ath ndipo sanamulole kuti akhale ndi mtendere mpaka atavomera “Koma ndikumva cisoni kwambiri ndi ana osaukawa, cimodzimodzi, adatero bamboyo.

text.S1: The two children had also not been able to sleep for hunger, and had heard what their stepmother had said to their father. Gretel wept bitter tears, and said to Hansel, “Now all is over for us.”“Hush,Gretel,” said Hansel, “do not distress yourself, I will soon find a way to help us.”
text.S2: The two children had also not been able to sleep for hunger, and had heard what their stepmother had said to their father. Gretel wept bitter tears, and said to Hansel, “Now all is over for us.”“Hush,Gretel,” said Hansel, “do not distress yourself, I will soon find a way to help us.”
text.T1: Ana awiri aja sanakwanitse kugona cifukwa ca njala, ndipo anamva zones zimene amayi awo wopeza ananena kwa atate awo. Gretel analira kwambiri ndipo misozi inagwa, ndipo anati kuli Hansel. “Kwaife tsopano kwatha.” “Khala cete, Gretel, anateroHansel, “osada nkhawa ayi, posacedwapa ndidzapeza njira mmene tingadzithandizire,”

text.S1: And when the old folks had fallen asleep, he got up, put on his little coat, opened the door below, and crept outside. The moon shone brightly, and the white pebbles which lay in front of the house glittered like real silver pennies.
text.S2: And when the old folks had fallen asleep, he got up, put on his little coat, opened the door below, and crept outside. The moon shone brightly, and the white pebbles which lay in front of the house glittered like real silver pennies.
text.T1: Ndipo pamene nkhalamba zinali gone, anawuka, ndikuvala khoti lake lopepuka, anatsekula citseko m’munsi, ndikutuluka panja. Mwezi unali unawala kwambiri, ndipo miyala yoyera imeneinali kutsogolo kwa nyumba inawala ngati ndalama zenizenizasiliva.
text.T2: Ndipo pamene nkhalamba zinali gone, anawuka, ndikuvala khoti lake locepekela, anatsekula citseko m’munsi, ndikutuluka panja. Mwezi unali unawala kwambiri, ndipo miyala yoyera imene inali kutsogolo kwa nyumba inawala ngati ndalama zenizeniza siliva.

text.S1: Hansel stooped and put as many of them in the little pocket of his coat as he could possiblyget in. Then he went back and said to Gretel, “Be comforted, dear little sister, and sleep in peace, God will not forsake us,” and he lay down again in his bed.
text.S2: Hansel stooped and put as many of them in the little pocket of his coat as he could possiblyget in. Then he went back and said to Gretel, “Be comforted, dear little sister, and sleep in peace, God will not forsake us,” and he lay down again in his bed.
text.T1: Hansel anawelama ndipo analongera m’thumba laling’ono la khoti lake momwe anakwanitsa. Ndipo anapita kwa Gretel, “Tonthozedwa mlongo wanga wokondedwa, ndipo gona mu mtendere, Mulungu sangatisiye,” ndipo Hansel anagonanso pa kama lake.

text.S1: When day dawned, but before the sun had risen, the woman came and awoke the two children, saying, “Get up, you sluggards! We are going into the forest to fetch wood.” She gave each a little piece of bread, and said, “There is something for your dinner, but do not eat it up before then, for you will get nothing else.”
text.T1: M’matanda kuca, koma dzuwa lisanatuluke mzimayi uja anabwera ndi kudzutsa ana awiri aja, kuti,” Dzukani, inu awulesi, tikupita m’nkhalango kukafuna nkhuni” Iye anapatsa aliyense kabuledi kakang’ono nati, “Pali cinacake cakudya madzulo, musadye msanga, cifukwa simudzapenso cina.”

text.S1: Gretel took the bread under her apron, as Hansel had the stones in his pocket. Then they all set out together on the way to the forest. When they had walked a short time, Hansel stood still and peeped back at the house, and did so again and again.
text.T1: Gretel anayikakabuledi ndi kukaika m’thumba la epulo lake, ndipo Hansel anali ndi miyala m’thumba lake. Pambuyo pake iwo onse ananyamuka ulendo wopita kunkhalango. Pamene anangoyenda nthawi yaing’ono, Hansel anaimirira ndikupenya kunyumba, ndipo anacita ici mobwerezerabwerezera.

text.S1: His father said, “Hansel, what are you looking at there and staying behind for? Mind yourself, and do not forget how to use your legs.”
text.T1: Atate ake anati, “Hansel, kodi ukupenya ciyani kumeneko ndipo ukukhalira ciyani kumbuyo?” Dziwa, ndipo osayiwala momwe umagwiritsira nchito miyendo yako.

text.S1: “Ah, father,” said Hansel, “I am looking at my little white cat, which is sitting up on the roof, and wants to say goodbye to me.” The wife said, “Fool, that is not your little cat, that is the morning sun which is shining on the chimneys.” Hansel, however, had not been looking back at the cat,but had been constantly throwing one of the white pebblestones out of his pocket on the road.
text.T1: “Aaaa atate,” anatero Hansel. “Ndikupenyakamphaka kanga koyera, kamene kali khale patsidwi ndipo kafuna kuyalirana nane. Mkazi anati, “Citsiru iwe, kameneko si kamphaka chona kako, limenelo ndi dzuwa la m’mawa lomwe likuwala potulukira utsi.” Komabe, Hansel, samapenyetsetsa kamphaka kake, koma amaponya miyala yoyera kucokera m’thumba m’msewu womwe anadzera.

text.S1: When they had reached the middle of the forest, the father said, “Now, children, pile up some wood, and I will light a fire that you may not be cold.” Hansel and Gretel gathered brushwood together, as high as a little hill.
text.T1: Pamene anafika pakati pankhalango, atate awo anati, “Tsopano, ana inu, unjikani nkhuni,ndipo ine ndidzayatsa moto kuti musamvere mphepo,” Hansel ndi Gretel anawunjika nkhuni pamodzi, pafupifupi ngati ka phiri kakang’ono.

text.S1: The brushwood was lighted, and when the flames were burning very high, the woman said, “Now,children, lay yourselves down by the fire and rest. We will go into the forest and cut some wood. When we have done, we will come back and fetch you away.”
text.T1: Moto wa nkhuni unayatsidwa, ndipo pamene malawi anayamba kuyaka kwambiri, mzimayi anati “Tsopano ana inu gonani mbali mwa moto ndipo mupumule. Ife tikupita m’khalango kukadula nkhuni.Tikatsiriza, tidzabweranso ndi kukutengani”

text.S1: Hansel and Gretel sat by the fire, and when noon came, each ate a little piece of bread,and as they heard the strokes of the wood-axe they believed that their father was near. It was not, however, the axe, it was a branch which he had fastened to a withered tree which the wind was blowing backwards and forwards. And as they had been sitting such a long time, their eyes shut with fatigue, and they fell fast asleep. When at last they awoke, it was already dark night.
text.T1: Hansel ndi Gretel anakhala m’mbali mwa moto, ndipo masana anafika, aliyense anadya kabuledi kakang’ono,ndipo pamene amamvera kutema kwa nkhuni anakhulupirira kuti atate awo anali pafupi. Komabe sizinali tero, ndipo nkhwangwa imene imamveka ngati ndi kutema nkhuni, inali nthambi imene inagwidwa kumtengo wouuma, imene imagunda kumtengo wowumawo cifukwa ca mphepo yomwe imawomba cakumbuyo ndi cakutsogolo. Ndipo pamene anali khale kwa nthawi yayitali, maso awo anatsekeka cifukwa cotopa ndipo anagona tulo tofanato. Pamene anadzuka potsirizira pake, kunali kale mdima.

text.S1: Gretel began to cry and said, “How are we to get out of the forest now?” But Hansel comforted her and said, “Just wait a little, until the moon has risen, and then we will soon find the way.” And when the full moon had risen, Hansel took his little sister by the hand, and followed the pebbles which shone like newly-coined silver pieces, and showed them the way.
text.T1: Gretel anayamba kulira nati “Tidzacoka bwanji m’nkhalango muno tsopano?” Koma Hansel anamukhazika mtima pansi kuti,“Yembekeza nthawi yocepa, mpaka mwezi utatuluka, ndipo tidzapeza njira mmene tingabwerere.” Ndipo pamene mwezi wathunthu unatuluka, Hansel anatenga mlongo wake wam’ng’ono pomgwira padzanja, ndikulondola miyala imeneinawala ngati ndalama zatsopano zasiliva ndipo inawaonetsa njira yobwerera kwawo.

text.S1: They walked the whole night long, and by break of day came once more to their father's house. They knocked at the door, and when the woman opened it and saw that it was Hansel and Gretel, she said, “You naughty children, why have you slept so long in the forest? We thought you were never coming back at all!”
text.T1: Iwo anayenda usiku wonse, ndipo pamene kunali kucha anali atafika panyumba ya atate awo. Anagogoda pacitseko, ndipo pamene mzimayi anatsekula anawona kuti anali Hansel ndi Gretel, nati,“Ana inu opusa, n’cifukwa ciyani mwagona nthawi yayitali kwambiri m’nkhalango? Timaganiza kuti mwina simudzabweranso!”

text.S1: The father,however, rejoiced, for it had cut him to the heart to leave them behind alone. Not long afterwards, there was once more great scarcity in all parts, and the children heard their mother saying at night to their father, “Everything is eaten again, we have one half loaf left,and after that there is no more. The children must go. We will take them farther into the wood, so that they will not find their way out again; there is no other means of saving ourselves!”
text.T1: Koma atate awo anakondwera, cifukwa anakhudzidwa mtima posiya ana okha.Pasanapite nthawi yaitali, kunasowanso cakudya m’mbali zonse, ndipo anamvera amayi awo akuuza atate awo kuti, “Ciliconse cadyedwa kale, tili ndi theka la buledi, ndipo sitidzakhalanso ndi cakudya cotsalira. Ana awa ayenera kupita. Tidzawapereka m’kati mwa nkhalango, kotero kuti sadzapeza njira yobwereranso; cifukwa palibe mwina mocitira kuti tidzipulumutse!”

text.S1: The man's heart was heavy, and he thought, “It would be better for you to share the last mouthful with your children.” The woman, however, would listen to nothing that he had to say, but scolded and reproached him. He who says what must say what, likewise, and as he had yielded the first time, he had to do so a second time also.
text.T1: Mtima wa munthuyo unali wolemera, ndipo anaganiza, “Zingakhale bwino kugawana cakudya ndi ana ako ngakhale kuti cakudyaco ndicothera. “Palibe ciliconsecimene mzimayi anamvera cimene mwamuna wakeangakambe, koma kumunyoza ndi kumdzudzula. Iye yemwe amalankhula zoyenera kucitika ayeneranso kulankhula, ndipo mofanana ndi poyamba kuti mwamuna anagonja, cotero, adzagonjanso.

text.S1: The children were, however, still awake and had heard the conversation. When the old folks were asleep,Hansel again got up, and wanted to go out and pick up pebbles as he had done before, but the woman had locked the door, and Hansel could not get out. Nevertheless, he comforted his little sister, and said, “Do not cry, Gretel, go to sleep quietly, the good God will help us.”
text.T1: Ngakhale zinali tero, ana aja anali asanagone, ndipo anali atamva zokambirana zonse. Pamene makolo anali cigonere,Hansel anadzuka, amafuna kukatenga miyala monga muja anacitira poyamba, koma mzimayi anali atakhoma kucitseko, ndipo Hansel sakanakwanitsa kutuluka.Ngakhale zinali tero, anauza mlongo wake kuti asade nkhawa,ndipo anati, “Osalira, Gretel, kagone mwakacetecete, Mulungu wabwino adzatithandiza”

text.S1: Early in the morning came the woman, and took the children out of their beds. Their bit of bread was given to them, but it was still smaller than the time before. On the way into the forest Hansel crumbled his in his pocket, and often stood still and threw a morsel on the ground. “Hansel, why do you stop and look round?” said the father, “go on.”
text.T1: M’mamawa mzimai anabwera, ndikudzutsa ana m’mabedi mwawo. Anapatsidwa buledi wocepa, koma unali wocepadipolinganiza ndi ujawakale. Ali paulendo wopita m’nkhalango Hansel ankapisa mthumba,ndipo amayimirira kawirikawiri ndikuponya tizidutswa pansi. “Hansel, n’cifukwa ciyani ukuimirira ndi kupenyapenya?” anatero atate ake, “tiye uziyenda”

text.S1: “I am looking back at my little pigeon which is sitting on the roof, and wants to say goodbye to me,"answered Hansel.
text.T1: “Ndikupenya kumbuyo kumene kuli kankhunda kanga kakang’ono komwe kali patsindwi, ndipo kakufuna kuti tiyalirane,” anayankha tero Hansel.

text.S1: “Simpleton!” said the woman, “that is not your little pigeon, that is the morning sun that is shining on the chimney.” Hansel, however, little by little, threw all the crumbs on the path.
text.T1: “Kupusa iwe” anatero mzimayi, “sikankhunda kako kakang’ono, kumeneko ndikuwala kwa dzuwa lomwe likuwonekera potulukira utsi,” Komabe Hansel, anapitirizakuponya tizidutswa m’njira.

text.S1: The woman led the children still deeper into the forest, where they had never in their livesbeen before. Then a great fire was again made, and the mother said, “Just sit there, you children, and when you are tired you may sleep a little; we are going into the forest to cut wood,and in the evening when we are done, we will come and fetch you away.”
text.T1: Mzimayi anatsogolera ana aja m’kati mwa nkhalango, komwe iwo sanapiteko pa moyo wawo. Pambuyo pake, moto waukulu unayatsidwa, ndipo amayi awo anati,” “Khalani pano, ana inu, ndipo ngati mwalema mungagoneko pang’ono; ife tikupita m’nkhalango kukadula nkhuni, ndipo m’madzulo tikatsiriza, tidzabwera kukutengani.”

text.S1: When it was noon, Gretel shared her piece of bread with Hansel, who had scattered his by the way. Then they fell asleep and evening came and went, but no one came to the poor children. They did not awake until it was dark night, and Hansel comforted his little sister and said, “Just wait, GretelI,until the moon rises, and then we shall see the crumbs of bread which I have strewn about, they will show us our way home again.”When sthe moon came they set out, but they found no crumbs...
text.T1: M’masana, Gretel anagawana bulediwake ndi Hansel, cifukwa iye anali atamwaza buledi wake m’njira monse. Pambuyo pake iwo anagona m’madzulo anafika, ndipo panalibe amene anabwera kudzafuna ana aja. Sanadzuke mpaka usiku, ndipo Hansel alimbikitsa mlongo wake kuti, “Yembekeza, Gretel, mpaka mwezi ukwereko ndipo tidzaona bwino tizidutswa tabuledi timene ndinaponya, timeneto tidzationetsa njira yopita kunyumba kaciwiri. “Pamene mwezi unawala ulendo wawo unayamba, koma sanapezetizidutswa tabuledi...

text.S1: For the many thousands of birds which fly about in the woods and fields had picked them all up. Hansel said to Gretel, “We shall soon find the way,” but they did not find it. They walked the whole night and all the next day too from morning till evening, but they did not get out of the forest, and were very hungry, for they had nothing to eat but two or three berries, which grew on the ground. And as they were so weary that their legs would carry them no longer, they lay down beneath a tree and fell asleep.
text.T1: Cifukwa ca zikwi zambiri za mbalame zomwe zinkauluka m’nkhalango ndi m’minda zinadya tizidutswa tabuledi timeneto. Hansel anati kwa Gretel, “Tidzapeza njira posacedwa,” koma sanaipeze. Iwo anayenda usiku wonse ndi m’mawa mwake kucokera m’mawa mpaka madzulo, koma sanatuluke m’nkhalango muja,ndipo anamva njala kwambiri, cifukwa cakuti analibe cakudya koma zipatso ziwiri kapena zitatu zamthengo zomwe zinkamera pansi. Ndipo cifukwa cakuti anali wofoka kwambiri kwakuti miyendo siikanatha kuyenda,anakhala m’munsi mwamtengo ndipo anagona.

text.S1: It was now three mornings since they had left their father's house. They began to walk again, but they always got deeper into the forest, and if help did not come soon, they would die of hunger and weariness. When it was midday, they saw a beautiful snow-white bird sitting on a bough, which sang so delightfully that they stood still and listened to it. And when it had finished its song, it spread its wings and flew away before them, and they followed it until they reached a little house, on the roof of which it alighted; and when they came quite up to the little house they saw that it was built of bread and covered with cakes, but that the windows were of clear sugar.
text.T1: Panali patapita masiku atatu pamene anacoka kunyumba ya atate awo. Iwo anayambanso kuyenda, koma iwo ankapita m’kati mwa nkhalango,ndipo ngati thandizo sanalipeze mwamsanga, akanafa ndi njala komanso kutopa. Pamene masana anafika,anawona mbalame yautoto ngati cipale cofewa ili khale pamtengo, imene imayimbamosangalatsa kotero kuti anaimirira ndi kuimvetsera. Ndipo pomwe itatha kuyimba nyimbo, inatambasula mapiko ake ndi kuwuluka, anayilondola mpaka anafika kanyumba, pamene inatera; ndipo atafika kufupi kwenikweni anawona kuti inali yomangidwa ndi buledi, ili yokutidwa ndi keke, ndipo mazenera ake anali wopangidwa ndi shuga wowala.

text.S1: “We will set to work on that,” said Hansel, “and have a good meal. I will eat a bit of the roof, and you, Gretel, can eat some of the window, it will taste sweet.” Hansel reached up above, and broke off a little of the roof to try how it tasted, and Gretel leaned against the window and nibbled at the panes. Then a soft voice cried from the room...
text.T1: “Tidzagwirirapo nchito” anatero Hansel, “ndipo tidzakhala ndi cakudya cabwino. Ine ndidzadya pang’ono tsindwi, iwe Gretel ungadyeko mazenera, ndipo ndiotsekemera.” Hansel anafika patsindwi ndi kuphwanya pang’ono tsindwi kuti amvere mmene imamvekera, ndipo Gretel anatsamira zenera ndi kubudulamagalasi.Mawu otsitsa anamveka kulira kucokera m’cipinda………

text.S1: “Nibble, nibble, gnaw,Who is nibbling at my little house?” The children answered,“The wind,the wind, The heaven-born wind,” and went on eating without disturbingthemselves. Hansel, who thought the roof tasted very nice, tore down a great piece of it, and Gretel pushed out the whole of one round windowpane, sat down, and enjoyed herself with it.
text.T1: “Budu, budu, tafuna, ndiwe ndani ukubudula kanyumba kanga kakang’ono?” Ana anayankha kuti, “Ndi mphepo, mphepo, Ndi mphepo yocokera kumwamba,” ndipo anapitiriza kudya mosazisokoneza iwo okha. Hansel, amene anaganiza kuti tsindwi linamveka bwino kwambiri, anang’amba cidutswa cacikulu, ndipo Gretel anakankha zenera lonse limodzi, nakhala pansi ndipo anayamba kudya ndipo anasangalala nalo.

text.S1: Suddenly the door opened, and a very, very old woman, who supported herself on crutches,came creeping out. Hansel and Gretel were so terribly frightened that they let fall what they had in their hands. The old woman, however, nodded her head, and said, “Oh, you dear children, who has brought you here? Do come in, and stay with me. No harm shall happen to you.” She took them both by the hand, and led them into her little house. Then good food was set before them, milk and pancakes, with sugar, apples, and nuts. Afterwards two pretty little beds were covered with clean white linen, and Hansel and Gretel lay down in them, and thought they were in heaven.
text.T1: Mwadzidzidzi citseko cinatsekuka, ndipo nkhalamba yaikazi, imeneinkayenda ndi ndodo, inatuluka cokwawa. Hansel ndi Gretel anagwidwa ndi mantha kwambiri kwakuti kuti anataya pansi kalikonse komwe anali nako m’manja. Amayi acikulire, ngakhale zinali tero, anavomera ndi mutu, nati, “Aaa, ana inu okondedwa, ndani amene wakubweretsani kuno? Lowani m’kati, ndipo mukhale ndi ine.Palibe coipa ciliconse cidzacitika kwa inu.” Iwo an aawagwira padzanja ana aja, ndi kuwatsogolera kukanyumba kawo kakang’ono.Pambuyo pake cakudya cabwino cinakonzedwa, mkaka ndi makeke, osakaniza ndi shuga, maapulo ndi nshawa. Zitatha izi, mabedi awiri owonekabwino ali oyalidwa bwino ndi nsalu zoyera, ndipo Hansel ndi Gretel anagona mmenemo, ndipo iwo anaganiza kuti anali kumwamba.

text.S1: The old woman had only pretended to be so kind; she was in reality a wicked. When a childcfell into her power, she killed it, cooked and ate it, and that was a feast day with her. Witcheshave red eyes, and cannot see far, but they have a keen scent like the beasts, and are awarewhen human beings draw near. When Hansel and Gretel came into her neigh- borhood,shelaughed maliciously, and said mockingly, “I have them, they shall not escape me again!”
text.T1: Mzimayi wokalamba amangoyeserera kuti ndi munthu wabwino; koma kunena zoona anali mfiti yamalaza. Pamene mwana wakhala m’manja mwake, amamupha, kuphika ndi kumudya ndipo linali tsiku laphwando. Mfiti zili ndi maso ofiira, ndipo sizipenya patali koma zili ndi fungo monga lanyama,lowopsa ndipo zimadziwa ngati munthu alipafupi. Pamene Hansel ndi Gretel anabwera ndi kukhala nawo, anaseka monyodola, nati mowaseka,” Ndili nawo, ndipo sadzathawanso!”

text.S1: Early in the morning before the children were awake, she was already up, and when shesaw both of them sleeping and looking so pretty, with their plump red cheeks, she mnuttered toherself, “That will be a dainty mouthful!” Then she seized Hansel with her shriveled hand,carried him into a little stable, and shut him in with a grated door. He might scream as he liked,that was of no use. Then she went to Gretel, shook her till she awoke, and cried, “Get up, lazything, fetch some water, and cook something good for your brother, he is in the stable outside,and is to be made fat. When he is fat, I will eat him.”
text.T1: M’mamawa anaaja asanauke,nkhalamba ija inali itauka kale, ndipo itawona onse ali gone ndipo akuwoneka bwino, masaya ofiira onenepa, anadzikambitsa yekha, “Mkamwa mwanga mudzakondwera.” Anagwira Hansel ndi dzanja lake lolemala, anamunyamula kupita naye m’khola ndikumtsekera ndi citseko colimba. Iye angalire mmene angachitire, koma zimenezo ndi zopanda phindu. Pambuyo pake nkhalamba ija inapita kwa Gretel, inamu‘gunduza m’paka anauka, ndipo analira, “Dzuka, iwe waulesi, ufune madzi, uphike cakudya cabwino ca mlongo wako, iye ali m’khola panja, ndipo ndzamunenepetsa. Pamene wanenepa, ndidzamudya.”

text.S1: Gretel began to weep bitterly, but it was all in vain; she was forced to do what the wicked witch ordered her.
text.T1: Gretel anayamba kulira kwambiri, koma palbe ciliconse cikanacitika;iye anakakamizidwa kucita cimene mzimai mfiti imafuna.

text.S1: And now the best food was cooked for poor Hansel, but Gretel got nothing but crab shells. Every morning the woman crept to the little stable, and cried, “Hansel, stretch out your finger that I may feel if you will soon be fat.” Hansel, however, stretched out a little bone to her, and the old woman, who had dim eyes, could not see it, and thought it was Hansel's finger, and was astonished that there was no way of fattening him.
text.T1: Tsopano cakudya cabwino cinaphikidwa ca Hansel,koma Gretel sanapatsidweko koma zigoba za nkhono cabe.M’mawa muli monse nkhalamba ija imalowa m’khola, ndipo ndikulira, “Hansel, tambasula cala cako kuti ndimvere ngati wanenepa. “Hansel, anatambasula kafupa kakang’ono,nkhalambayo, maso ake amapenya nkhungu, samawona bwino ayi, ndipo amaganiza kuti ndi cala ca Hansel, ndipo anadabwa kuti panalibe njira yakuti anganenepe.

text.S1: When four weeks had gone by, and Hansel still stayed thin, she was seized with impatience and would not wait any longer. “Now, Gretel,” she cried to the girl, “be active, and bring some water.Let Hansel be fat or lean tomorrow I kill him and cook him.”
text.T1: Patapita milunguinayi, ndipo Hansel anakhalabe wowonda,nkhalamba inakhala yotekeseka ndipo siinafune kuyembekezera kwa nthawi yayitali... “Tsopano, Gretel,” nkhalamba ija inakwezera mawu mtsikana, “Ufunika kusamalakwambiri, ndipo bweretsa madzi. Hansel afunika kunenepa cifukwa mawa ndidzamupha ndikum’phika.”

text.S1: Ah, how the poor little sister did lament when she had to fetch the water, and how her tearsdid flow down over her cheeks! “Dear God, do help us,” she cried. “If the wild beasts in theforest had devoured us, at least we should have died together.”
text.T1: Oho,mlongo wake anadandaula pamene amafuna madzi ndipo misozi inkagwa m’matsaya ake. “Mulungu wokondedwa, tithandizeni,”analira. “Ngati zilombo zikanatidya m’nkhalango, mwinamwake tinakafera pamodzi”

text.S1: “Just keep your noise to yourself,” said the old woman, “all that won't help you at all.” Early in the morning, Gretel had to go out and hang up the cauldron with the water, and light the fire. “We will bake first,” said the old woman. “I have al- ready heated the oven, and kneaded the dough.” She pushed poor Gretel out to the oven, from which flames of fire were already darting. “Creep in,” said the witch, “and see if it is properly heated, so that we can shut the bread in.”And once Gretel was inside, she intended to shut the oven and let her bake in it, and then she would eat her,too.
text.T1: “Sunga phokoso lako kwa iwe mwini,” inatero nkhalamba ija, “palibe ciliconse cimene cidzakuthandiza iwe.”M’mamawa kuli mbuu,Gretel anapita kukapacika ndowa mosungira madzi ndi kuyatsa moto. “Poyamba tidzapanga buledi,” inatero nkhalamba.” Mophikira mwatentha kale, ndipo fulawulo wakonzedwa kale. Anam’kankhira m’ng’anjo yamoto momwe munali moto ndipo malawi amoto anali lawilawi. “Lowa mkati,” inatero mfiti yaikazi, “kuti uwone ngati moto wakondera, kuti tiyikemo buledi.” Nkhalambayo imafuna kuti ngati Gretel walowa, itseke ng’anjo kuti aphikike m’kati, ndipo kuti imudye nayenso.

text.S1: But Gretel saw what she had in her mind, and said, “l do not know how l am to do it; how do you get in?”
text.T1: Koma Gretel anali atadziwa zomwe nkhalambayo imaganiza, ndipo anati, “Sindidziwa mocitira;kodi ndingalowe bwanji?”

text.S1: “Silly goose,” said the old woman, “The door is big enough; just look, I can get in myself!”and she crept up and thrust her head into the oven. Then Gretel gave her a push that drove her far into it, and shut the iron door, and fastened the bolt. Oh! then she began to howl quite terribly,but Gretel ran away,andthe godless witch was miserably burnt to death.
text.T1: “Mwana wopusa wa tsekwe iwe,” nkhalamba ijainatero, “Citseko ici ndicacikulu; tapenya iwe, ine ndingalowe tere!” nkhalambayo inalowa m’kati ndi kudzikankhira m’ng’anjo.Ndipo Gretel anayikankha mwamphavu nkhalambayo,ndipo anatseka citseko cacitsulo, ndikumanga mabauti. Yaaa,nkhalamba inabuula kwambiri, koma Gretel anathawa ndipo mfiti yosakhulupira mulungu inafa ndi moto.

text.S1: Gretel,however, ran like lightning to Hansel, opened his littlestable, and cried,“Hansel,we are saved! The old witch is dead!” Then Hansel sprang out like a bird from its cage when the door was opened for it. How they did rejoice and embrace each other, and dance about and kiss each other! And as they had no longer any need to fear her, they went into the witch's house, and in every corner there stood chests full of pearls and jewels.
text.T1: Gretel, anathamanga ngati mphezi kwa Hansel, anatsekula khola nalira, “Tapulumuka Hansel, nkhalamba mfiti yafa”Hansel anatuluka monga mbalame yomwe inali yomangidwa pamene chitseko chitatsekuka.Anakondwera ndi kugwirana canza,anavina ndi kupsopsonana. Panalibe chomwe angayope tsopano, analowa m’nyumba ya mfiti, ngodya zonse munali zinthu zamtengo wapatali.

text.S1: “These are far better than pebbles!” said Hansel, and thrust into his pockets whatever could be got in, and Gretel said, “I, too, will take something home with me,” and filled her pinafore full. “But now we will go away,” said Hansel, “that we may get out of the witch's forest.” When they had walked for two hours, they came to a great body of water. “We cannot get over,” said Hansel, “I see no foot-plank, and no bridge.” “And no boat crosses either,” answered Gretel,
text.T1: “Izi ndi zinthu zosiyana ndi miyala ija” anatero Hansel, ndipo anaiponyera m’thumba mwake ndi kali konse angakwanitse, ndipo Gretel anati, “Nanenso, ndidzanyamulako zinthu zimenezi kunyumba,”anadzaza thumba lake. “Tsopano tingayambepo”, “ticoke m’nkhalango ya mfiti.” Atayenda maola awiri anapeza dziwe lamadzi. “Sitingadutse ife apa,”anatero Hansel.” “Sindiwona powolokera, kapena ulalo,” “Kapena bwato kudutsa,” anayankha Gretel.

text.S1: “but a white duck is swimming there; if I ask her, she will help us over.” Then she cried...
text.T1: “Koma ndawona bakha woyera anyaya, mwina ndimufunse, mwina angatithandize kudutsa,” ndipo analira.

text.S1: “Little duck,little duck, do you see, Hansel and Gretel are waiting for you? There's never a plank, or bridge in sight, Take us across on your back so white.”
text.T1: “Iwe bakha, iwe bakha wamng’ono, tapenya kuno, Hansel ndi Gretel alukuyembekezerani? Palibe thabwa kapena ulalo pano. Tibaphekoni?”

text.S1: The duck came to them, and Hansel seated himself on its back, and told his sister to sit by him. “No,” replied Gretel, “that will be too heavy for the little duck; she shall take us across, one after the other.” The good little duck did so, and when they were safely across and had walked for a short time, the forest seemed to be more and more familiar to them, and at length they saw from afar their father's house. Then they began to run, rushed into the parlor, and threw themselves into their father's arms. The man had not known one happy hour since he had left the children in the forest; the woman, however, was dead. Gretel emptied her pinafore until pearls and precious stones ran about the room, and Hansel threw one handful after another out of his pocket to add to them. Then all anxiety was at an end, and they lived together in perfect happiness. My tale is done, see the mouse run, whoever catches it, may make himself a big fur cap out of it.
text.T1: Bakha anabwera,Hansel anakhala kumbuyo, anawuza mlongosi wake kuti akhale m’mbali mwake,” “Ayi,” anayankha Gretel,sadzakwanitsa kutinyamula tawiri;ndikwabwino atinyamule m’modzi m’modzi.Kabakha ka kanakwaniritsa, ndipo anali kumtunda, ndipo atayenda kwa nthawi yaying’ono, anayamba kuzindikira nkhalango, ndipo pamene anali patali anawona nyumba ya atate awo. Anayamba kuthamanga,analowa m’kati, ndikudziponya m’manja mwa atate awo. Atate awo sanapeze mtendere pamene iwo anasiya ana aja m’nkhalango;mzimayi woipa uja anali atafa kale. Gretel anatulutsa zomwe ananyamula zamtengo wapatali nathamangira m’cipinda, ndipo Hansel anatulutsa zomwe anatenga nayenso kuwonjezera pazomwe mlongo wake anabweretsa. Nkhawa inatha, ndipo anayamba kukhalanso bwino. Nkhani yanga yatha, onani khoswe akuthamanga, aliyense angagwire, anagapange kapu yaubweya.
